# Part A

1. Bibliographic coupling; corpus documents; `CR`.
2. Reference co-citation; cited references; `CR`.
3. Co-word thematic mapping; terms; `DE`, `ID`, or `KW_Merged`.
4. Country collaboration; affiliation countries; `C1` or `AU_CO`.
5. Thematic evolution plus term growth; terms and `PY`.
6. Historiography; direct citations; `CR`, `PY`, and document identifiers.

# Parts B–G: Reference workflow

```{r}
#| label: solutions-setup

source(here::here("R", "00_setup.R"))
M <- load_demo_data()

dim(M)
range(M$PY)

audit_fields <- c("DE", "ID", "AB", "CR", "C1", "DI")
M |>
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(audit_fields),
      ~ sum(!is.na(.x) & nzchar(trimws(as.character(.x))))
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "field", values_to = "available") |>
  mutate(
    total = nrow(M),
    percent_available = round(100 * available / total, 1)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: solutions-duplicates

sum(duplicated(M$DI[!is.na(M$DI)]))
sum(duplicated(paste(tolower(M$TI), M$PY)))
```

If `CR` is substantially missing, coupling, co-citation, local-citation, and historiographic analyses become incomplete and potentially biased.

The acronym mappings such as `rct`, `ckd`, and `ibd` require corpus-context review because an acronym can be ambiguous outside a narrowly defined biomedical corpus. A mapping should be removed when the same abbreviation is used for more than one concept.

```{r}
#| label: solutions-keywords

M <- bibliometrix::mergeKeywords(M, force = TRUE)

keyword_fields <- c("DE", "ID", "KW_Merged")
M |>
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(keyword_fields),
      ~ sum(!is.na(.x) & nzchar(trimws(as.character(.x))))
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "field", values_to = "available") |>
  mutate(
    total = nrow(M),
    percent_available = round(100 * available / total, 1)
  )
```

The drug name is removed from clustering because it occurs across the corpus and contributes little discrimination. It remains part of eligibility and the raw data.

```{r}
#| label: solutions-performance

annual <- M |> count(PY)

ggplot(annual, aes(PY, n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7fb8")

M |>
  mutate(period = cut(PY, c(2007, 2013, 2018, 2022, 2025))) |>
  count(period, INDICATION)
```

```{r}
#| label: solutions-citations

M |>
  mutate(
    citation_window = pmax(1, 2025 - PY + 1),
    citations_per_year = TC / citation_window
  ) |>
  group_by(PY) |>
  mutate(
    year_mean_tc = mean(TC, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_normalised_tc = if_else(
      year_mean_tc > 0,
      TC / year_mean_tc,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(desc(citations_per_year)) |>
  select(SR, PY, TC, citations_per_year) |>
  head(10)
```

Citation counts reflect exposure time, database coverage, visibility, document type, and citation practices. They do not directly measure risk of bias or clinical validity.

```{r}
#| label: solutions-thematic

tm <- bibliometrix::thematicMap(
  M = M,
  field = "KW_Merged",
  n = 100,
  minfreq = 5,
  ngrams = 1,
  stemming = FALSE,
  size = 0.7,
  n.labels = 3,
  community.repulsion = 0,
  repel = TRUE,
  remove.terms = fcm_remove_terms,
  synonyms = fcm_synonyms,
  cluster = "louvain",
  subgraphs = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.5,
  seed = 20261126
)
tm$map
tm$clusters
tm$words |>
  arrange(Cluster, desc(Cluster_PageRank), desc(Occurrences)) |>
  group_by(Cluster, Cluster_Label) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| label: solutions-thematic-de

tm_de$map
```

Field choice may change term coverage, cluster membership, labels, and quadrant positions. The substantive interpretation should focus on themes stable across defensible specifications.

```{r}
#| label: solutions-evolution

te <- bibliometrix::thematicEvolution(
  M,
  field = "KW_Merged",
  years = c(2013, 2018, 2022),
  n = 100,
  minFreq = 3,
  remove.terms = fcm_remove_terms,
  synonyms = fcm_synonyms,
  cluster = "louvain",
  seed = 20261126
)

bibliometrix::plotThematicEvolution(te$Nodes, te$Edges, min.flow = 0.10)
```

```{r}
#| label: solutions-overlays

theme_columns <- intersect(tm$clusters$name, names(tm$documentToClusters))

membership_long <- tm$documentToClusters |>
  select(SR, all_of(theme_columns)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(theme_columns),
    names_to = "theme",
    values_to = "membership"
  )

membership_long |>
  left_join(M |> select(SR, INDICATION), by = "SR") |>
  filter(!is.na(INDICATION)) |>
  group_by(theme, INDICATION) |>
  summarise(weighted_documents = sum(membership, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(theme) |>
  mutate(percent_within_theme = 100 * weighted_documents / sum(weighted_documents)) |>
  ungroup()

membership_long |>
  left_join(M |> select(SR, FUNDING_TYPE), by = "SR") |>
  filter(!is.na(FUNDING_TYPE)) |>
  group_by(theme, FUNDING_TYPE) |>
  summarise(weighted_documents = sum(membership, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(theme) |>
  mutate(percent_within_theme = 100 * weighted_documents / sum(weighted_documents)) |>
  ungroup()
```

The funding analysis describes how disclosed categories are distributed across themes. It does not establish that funding caused a theme, outcome, or publication decision.

# Part H: Model methods paragraph

Bibliographic records were converted to a standard bibliographic data frame and audited for missing fields and duplicates. Author and indexed keywords were merged and harmonised using a prespecified synonym dictionary. Query-defining FCM terms were excluded from clustering because they did not discriminate among topics. A co-word thematic map was generated from `KW_Merged`, retaining 100 terms and using a `minfreq` value of 5. The association-strength-normalised network was clustered using the Louvain algorithm with a fixed seed of 20261126. Themes were positioned according to centrality and density. Automatic cluster labels were checked against the ten highest-ranking terms and high-membership documents. Sensitivity analyses repeated the map using author keywords, alternative term counts, frequency thresholds, and Leiden clustering. Package versions and returned parameter tables were retained.

Files to archive include raw exports, search log, screening decisions, cleaning dictionary, analysis scripts, parameter register, derived membership tables, figures, and `sessionInfo()`.
